title: Cinema Seat Allocation
summary: A cinema has n rows of seats, with each row containing 10 seats numbered from 1 to 10.
statement: A cinema has n rows of seats, with each row containing 10 seats numbered from 1 to 10. A 2D integer array, reservedSeats, specifies which seats are already reserved. A four-person group must be seated in a block of four consecutive unreserved seats within the same row. The possible blocks are seats 2, 3, 4, 5; seats 4, 5, 6, 7; and seats 6, 7, 8, 9. Each seat can be assigned to at most one group. The task is to determine the maximum number of four-person groups that can be seated.
constraints: Each four-person family occupies seats 2-5, 4-7, or 6-9 in one row.
Rows without relevant reservations fit two families.
hints: Only reservations in seats 2 through 9 affect family blocks.
Encode each affected row as a bit mask; untouched rows contribute two.
For an affected row, test left 2-5, middle 4-7, and right 6-9; two fit only when both outer blocks fit.
These are the only allowed blocks, so the case analysis is exhaustive.
editorial: These are the only allowed blocks, so the case analysis is exhaustive.

tests.explanation: Rows one and two fit one family each; row three fits two.
Outer aisle seats do not matter, and valid blocks are checked independently.
